chapter: CHAPTER 1 — Three Eruptions That Changed a Continent
text: About two point one million years ago, the land where Yellowstone sits tore open. The Huckleberry Ridge eruption threw out roughly two thousand four hundred cubic kilometers of rock and ash. That's enough to bury the whole state of Rhode Island nearly half a mile deep. Its ash has been found as far away as sea-floor cores off California, part of a single ash layer traced across about three thousand kilometers.
